artists.biography: Nathan Fake is an English electronic musician from Necton, Norfolk. He first gained attention through releases on James Holden's Border Community label, particularly the single "The Sky Was Pink" (2004), whose remix by Holden proved influential and attracted sustained attention over two years. Fake has released seven studio albums across four labels—Border Community, Ninja Tune, his own Cambria Instruments, and InFiné—and has remixed artists including Radiohead, Jon Hopkins, and Sasha. He co-founded Cambria Instruments with Wesley Matsell in 2014. His work has been generally well received by critics, with his debut Drowning in a Sea of Love (2006) his most acclaimed release.

perplexity.description:
Evaporator is Nathan Fake's seventh studio album and his debut on the Paris-based InFiné label, marking a significant artistic shift after several years of silence. Conceived as "airy daytime music," the record represents a luminous turn away from the nocturnal and rave-driven atmospheres of his previous work, instead exploring vast, organic soundscapes that blend deep electronics, ambient techno, and more accessible melodic touches. Written during the summer of 2024 and completed in just six weeks, the album was crafted using Fake's characteristic instinctive approach—mostly recorded in single takes on Cubase with vintage production tools, including synths and even a toy Casio keyboard on the standout track "Yucon."

The eleven-track album showcases thrilling eclecticism across its runtime, ranging from the uplifting chords of "Aiwa" to the trance-inflected propulsion of "Hypercube," the widescreen ambience of "Sunlight on Saturn," and the loping disco beauty of the nine-minute closing track "Slow Yamaha." Fake employs clever production techniques throughout, including re-tuning Cubase software to create twisted yet functional shapes from classic rave and trance elements, while maintaining a lighter, poppier aesthetic than his earlier work. The album features two notable collaborations—"Baltasound" with Dextro, which creates a massive pillar of sound with reassuring depth, and "Orbiting Meadows" with Clark, featuring microtonal 18EDO piano and wailing pads.

After more than two decades defining a distinctive space within UK electronic music through soaring melodies and emotional openness, Evaporator reaffirms Nathan Fake's commitment to sonic exploration while marking a new chapter in his artistic journey. The record balances introspection with expansiveness, moving from vibrant sunbursts to bracing rainscapes and fine mists of clement melodics, proving his continued necessity as a leading figure in contemporary electronic music.
